findings.title: Account switching can display the previous user's private ethical medicine stock or marketplace exchanges before session-specific data is cleared.
findings.scenario: Alice has private ethical-stock inventory, listing drafts and marketplace conversations open in a Next tab. In another tab, Bob signs in and the shared session-provider sets this tab to loading then authenticated as Bob. The marketplace components retain Alice's contexts and rows. EthicalWorkspaceV2 hides loading only when contexts is empty, and its getAccess callbacks are not bound to user/session generation. GoodsWorkspace can render old exchanges while reloading; GoodsListingsV2 preserves old rows and access even after Bob's getAccess/dashboard request fails. Bob may momentarily or persistently see Alice's private item names, batches, transfers, listings or messages in the existing tab even though backend requests for Bob would be forbidden.
findings.confidence: high for source-retained-state render possibility; account-switch timing and live UX untested
findings.test_needed: Two unrelated owner accounts A/B with separate ethical inventories, goods listings and exchanges. Open A's private pages in tab1, log in as B in tab2 while tab1 remains mounted; simulate slow B getAccess and 403/error, and delay old A promises to finish last. Assert tab1 never renders A names, stock levels or messages once B is authenticated; confirm B sees only permitted data on success and old rows are purged immediately on session change. Repeat with same-tab account switch and logout/reauth.
